newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/Bund spread can easily dip below zero -dealers.
newsitem.headline: OLO/Bund spread can easily dip below zero -dealers.

text.p: The yield spread between Belgian 10-year linear bonds and their Bund equivalents could easily slip below zero in the near future on the back of further institutional buying of the major Belgian banks, dealers said.
"It can easily go to zero, go minus five," one trader in Luxembourg said.
At 0930 GMT, the yield premium of OLOs over Bunds was three basis points after earlier reaching two bp, against four at the close on Tuesday.
"A lot of Belgian banks cannot switch, have to buy Belgian paper and are loaded with cash for the moment," the dealer said.
The trader noted that the yield spread was already negative for most OLOs up to nine years.

Traders said that the OLO market was fired in similar fashion as the Bel-20 index of leading shares, which breached the crucial 2,000-point level earlier on Wednesday. "In the share market it's insurers. In the OLO market, the big banks are investing, mainly in paper with longer maturities," one said.
Traders noted OLO 24 (2006)-OLO 12 (2012) switching which they said sparked some "serious flattening" of the yield curve.
But one noted that compared with France, the OLO 12 could still be considered a bargain.
"(The OLO 12) can still go further than this," the trader noted.
He said that business had calmed down after a busy morning but noted that the market would start panicking again as soon as one of the banks re-emerged for multi-billion franc purchases.
At 1010 GMT, the new benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.78 percent against 5.77 earlier in the morning and 5.81 percent at the close on Tuesday.
